- Minneapolis Guaranteed Basic Income Pilot (Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; 2022–2024): Run by City of Minneapolis, paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA); the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis evaluated it. $500 a month with no conditions for 24 months (June 2022–June 2024) to 200 low-income households in nine Minneapolis ZIP codes, chosen at random; 329 others were a control group paid $150 per survey. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA). Result: A Minneapolis Fed working paper (December 2024, randomized, 200 recipients vs 329 controls) reported that the payments improved food security, housing stability and financial security, mental health and self-reported well-being while they lasted, with no effect on work; attrition differed between groups, which the authors adjusted for. Source: https://www.minneapolismn.gov/government/programs-initiatives/basic-income ; https://www.minneapolisfed.org/research/institute-working-papers/how-do-lowincome-households-respond-to-basic-income-experimental-evidence-from-minneapolis
- Guaranteed Income for Artists (Creatives Rebuild New York) (New York State, USA; 2022–2024): Run by Creatives Rebuild New York (CRNY), an artist-support initiative funded mainly by the Andrew W. Mellon Foundation, with the Stavros Niarchos and Ford foundations. $1,000 a month with no conditions for 18 months to 2,400 low-income artists in the state, enrolled in staggered groups from June 2022 (last payments March 2024), picked by a weighted lottery from more than 22,000 applicants. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: Indiana University researchers (Journal of Cultural Economics, accepted 2026) compared recipients with applicants not selected: about 3.9 more hours a week on arts work and 2.4 fewer on other work. Total earnings were about $11,600 a year lower, close to the $12,000 paid, but the authors say they cannot confidently attribute this to the program because artists' incomes vary so much. Source: https://fromcommonground.com/we-studied-what-happened-when-financially-struggling-artists-received-1000-a-month-no-strings-attached-for-18-months/ ; https://hyperallergic.com/954975/how-does-guaranteed-income-impact-artists-lives-creatives-rebuild-new-york/
- Ithaca Guaranteed Income (Ithaca, New York, USA; 2022–2023): Run by City of Ithaca, with Mayors for a Guaranteed Income, paid from private grants from nonprofit organizations and studied by Penn's Center for Guaranteed Income Research. $450 a month with no conditions on a prepaid card for 12 months (June 2022–May 2023) to 110 low-income unpaid caregivers of children or of older or disabled adults. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://guaranteedincome.us/ithaca ; https://wskg.org/ithaca-guaranteed-basic-income-pilot-rollout/
- Montgomery County Boost (Guaranteed Income Pilot) (Montgomery County, Maryland, USA; 2022–2025): Run by Montgomery County government (Department of Health and Human Services), paid from county funds with the Meyer Foundation and the Greater Washington Community Foundation. $800 a month with no conditions for 24 months to 300 households, 100 leaving homelessness and 200 families with children, enrolled in phases from June to November 2022. Funding: Public (city, county or state), Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://assets.montgomerycountymd.gov/files/council/resources/files/agenda/col/2023/20230511/20230511_32.pdf
- In Her Hands (Atlanta (Old Fourth Ward), College Park and rural Southwest Georgia, USA; 2022–2024): Run by Georgia Resilience and Opportunity Fund (GRO Fund), a nonprofit, with GiveDirectly delivering the money from a $13 million privately raised budget. $20,400 over two years with no conditions ($850 a month, or $4,300 up front then $700 a month) from mid-2022 to 654 low-income Black women in Atlanta's Old Fourth Ward, College Park and rural Southwest Georgia, chosen by lottery. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: A Washington University study in Health Affairs (February 2026) compared recipients with women not selected: 40% reported high or marginal food security vs 14%, with better diet quality, and the gains grew in the second year. Source: https://policiesforaction.org/blog/her-hands-path-financial-security-black-women-georgia ; https://atlanta.capitalbnews.org/guaranteed-income-atlanta
- Chicago Resilient Communities Pilot (Chicago, Illinois, USA; 2022–2023): Run by City of Chicago (Department of Family and Support Services), paid from federal pandemic relief money in the Chicago Recovery Plan; GiveDirectly delivered the payments. $500 a month with no conditions for 12 months (from July 2022) to 5,000 low-income households chosen by lottery from more than 176,000 applicants. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://harris.uchicago.edu/news-events/news/uchicago-inclusive-economy-lab-releases-first-report-chicago-resilient-communities ; https://chirecoveryplan.com/programs/chicago-resilient-communities-pilot/
- West Hollywood Pilot for Guaranteed Income (West Hollywood, California, USA; 2022–2024): Run by City of West Hollywood with the National Council of Jewish Women, Los Angeles; evaluated by Penn's Center for Guaranteed Income Research. $1,000 a month with no conditions for 18 months (August 2022–January 2024) to 25 randomly selected low-income residents aged 50 and older. Funding: Public (city, county or state). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.penncgir.org/weho-pilot-westhollywood-ca ; https://guaranteedincome.us/west-hollywood
- Baltimore Young Families Success Fund (Baltimore, Maryland, USA; 2022–2024): Run by City of Baltimore under Mayor Brandon Scott, paid from $4.8 million of federal pandemic relief (ARPA) and foundation money, administered by the CASH Campaign of Maryland. $1,000 a month with no conditions for 24 months (August 2022–July 2024) to 200 young parents aged 18–24, chosen at random from more than 4,000 applicants. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA), Philanthropic. Result: The final evaluation (October 2025), compared with 156 controls: 56% of recipients were food insecure at 18 months vs 72% of controls, and recipients missed about 9 fewer hours of work a month by the end. Abt Global's interim brief (June 2024) found 27% had applied to college or trade school at 12 months vs 13% of controls. Source: https://baltimorefishbowl.com/?p=222403 ; https://www.abtglobal.com/files/insights/reports/2024/baltimore-mgi-report-6.26.24.pdf
- Madison Forward Fund (Madison, Wisconsin, USA; 2022–2023): Run by City of Madison, with payments funded entirely by private donors including Mayors for a Guaranteed Income and local foundations. $500 a month with no conditions for 12 months (September 2022–August 2023) to 155 low-income Madison households with children, chosen at random from about 3,000 applicants. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.cityofmadison.com/node/24981 ; https://guaranteedincome.us/madison/
- Austin Guaranteed Income Pilot (Austin, Texas, USA; 2022–2023): Run by City of Austin with the nonprofit UpTogether, paid from $1.14 million of city money plus St. David's Foundation for 50 households. $1,000 a month with no conditions for 12 months (September 2022–August 2023) to 135 low-income households facing housing insecurity. Funding: Public (city, county or state), Philanthropic. Result: The Urban Institute (2024) surveyed 54 of the 135 households: they spent about 60% of the money on rent or mortgage, 14% more caught up on housing payments and 12% fewer felt at risk of eviction; mental health improved at six months but was back near baseline at 12; no control group. Source: https://communityimpact.com/austin/south-central-austin/government/2024/02/15/austin-families-given-1000-a-month-spent-most-of-it-on-housing-survey-finds ; https://austinmonitor.com/stories/2024/02/austin-gave-families-1000-a-month-for-a-year-most-of-the-money-was-spent-on-housing/
- Denver Basic Income Project (Denver, Colorado, USA; 2022–2024): Run by The Denver Basic Income Project, a nonprofit, funded by foundations, donors and $2 million of the City of Denver's federal pandemic relief (ARPA) money. $1,000 a month for a year (or $6,500 up front then $500 a month) with no conditions, from late 2022, to people experiencing homelessness in Denver; 807 enrolled across the two cash groups and a comparison group that got $50 a month. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA), Philanthropic. Result: The University of Denver's year-one report (June 2024) reported that about 45% of participants across all three groups were renting or owning a home at 10 months, nights in shelters halved in the two cash groups, and full-time work rose in those groups while falling in the $50 group; stress was slightly higher at the end. Source: https://hpri.usc.edu/homeless_research/denver-basic-income-project-year-one-evaluation-report/ ; https://coloradosun.com/2024/06/19/homeless-payments/
- Silicon Valley Guaranteed Income Project (Santa Clara County, California, USA; 2022–2024): Run by Destination: Home, a Silicon Valley nonprofit working on homelessness, with community partners and tech-industry and foundation donors. $1,000 a month with no conditions for two years to 150 Santa Clara County families with children who were homeless or at risk of homelessness, starting in December 2022. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://destinationhomesv.org/news/2022/11/30/1000-a-month-no-strings-attached-anti-poverty-experiment-comes-to-silicon-valley/ ; https://destinationhomesv.org/guaranteed-income/silicon-valley-guaranteed-income/
- Elevate MV (Mountain View, California, USA; 2022–2024): Run by City of Mountain View, run by the nonprofit Community Services Agency, with technical help from Mayors for a Guaranteed Income. $500 a month with no conditions for two years (December 2022–November 2024) to 166 extremely low-income Mountain View families with children, chosen at random; 132 other applicants formed a control group. Funding: Public (city, county or state). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://guaranteedincome.us/mountain-view ; https://www.mv-voice.com/poverty/2024/01/16/guaranteed-income-pilot-program-eases-financial-hardships-for-mountain-view-residents/
- Cook County Promise Guaranteed Income Pilot (Cook County, Illinois, USA; 2022–2025): Run by Cook County government (which includes Chicago), paid from $42 million of federal pandemic relief (ARPA); the University of Chicago Inclusive Economy Lab runs the evaluation. $500 a month with no conditions for two years (December 2022–January 2025) to 3,250 low-to-moderate-income households chosen by lottery from more than 233,000 applicants. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.cookcountyil.gov/promise ; https://arpa.cookcountyil.gov/promise-guaranteed-income-pilot-program
- Evanston Guaranteed Income Pilot Program (Evanston, Illinois, USA; 2022–2023): Run by City of Evanston with Northwestern University, paid from the city's federal pandemic relief (ARPA) money, Northwestern and the Evanston Community Foundation. $500 a month on a prepaid debit card with no conditions for 12 months (December 2022–November 2023) to 150 low-income young adults, seniors and undocumented residents chosen by lottery. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA), Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://dailynorthwestern.com/2023/01/18/lateststories/271409/ ; https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/ILEVANSTON/bulletins/33ae8da
- Rise Up Alameda (Alameda, California, USA; 2023–2025): Run by City of Alameda, paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA). $1,000 a month with no conditions for two years (2023–December 2025) to 150 low-income Alameda households chosen by lottery; 180 randomly selected applicants formed a control group. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA). Result: Abt Global's one-year interim report (2025) reported that, compared with the control group, fewer recipients were going into debt (15% vs 42%), more had money left at month's end (13% vs 1%) and nearly twice as many had $500+ saved, with lower stress; no negative effect on employment and no significant housing change. Source: https://www.kqed.org/news/12053655/alamedas-rise-up-pilot-shows-cash-aid-improves-financial-stability-mental-health ; https://alamedapost.com/news/alamedas-guaranteed-income-recipients-see-improvements-finances-beyond/
- Guaranteed Income for Artists (Springboard for the Arts) (Saint Paul and Otter Tail County, Minnesota, USA; 2023–): Run by Springboard for the Arts, a Saint Paul arts nonprofit, paid for by private foundations. $500 a month with no strings attached to 75 artists in Saint Paul and Otter Tail County from 2023, first for 18 months and then extended to five years ($30,000 each), with 25 more rural artists added in 2025 for 100 in total. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2024/11/29/in-minnesota-a-no-strings-attached-cash-programme-for-artists-is-gaining-momentum ; https://springboardforthearts.org/press/guaranteed-income-pilot-for-artists-in-axios-twin-cities/
- St. Louis Guaranteed Basic Income Pilot (St. Louis, Missouri, USA; 2023–2025): Run by City of St. Louis (Treasurer's Office), paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA) and a $1 million gift from Jack Dorsey; donors finished it after a lawsuit froze public funds. $500 a month with no conditions for 18 months (late 2023–May 2025, paused by a court order in July 2024) to 540 low-income families with school-age children, chosen by lottery from more than 5,000 applicants. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA), Philanthropic. Result: Washington University's Brown School (December 2025) reported fewer missed rent and utility payments and less food insecurity (family surveys), and credit scores up 12 points on average versus similar St. Louis residents who were not paid (193 consented to credit tracking); not a randomized trial, and the 2024 payment pause coincided with a dip in credit health. Source: https://source.washu.edu/2025/12/st-louis-guaranteed-basic-income-pilot-improved-financial-stability-study-finds/ ; https://www.stlpr.org/economy-business/2025-12-08/basic-income-pilot-families-financial-strain-washington-university-lawsuit-tornado-st-louis-missouri
- New Haven guaranteed income pilot for formerly incarcerated people (New Haven, Connecticut, USA; 2023–2024): Run by The nonprofit 4-CT, with the City of New Haven and the Project M.O.R.E. reentry center. $500 a month with no conditions on a prepaid card for a year to 20 people aged 25–55 recently released from prison, with reentry support. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://ctpublic.org/2023-03-28/20-formerly-incarcerated-individuals-will-receive-guaranteed-income-for-a-year-in-new-haven
- Guaranteed Income for Trans People (GIFT) (San Francisco, California, USA; 2023–2024): Run by City of San Francisco, run with Lyon-Martin Community Health Services (a clinic for trans, nonbinary and intersex people) and the Transgender District. Up to $1,200 a month with no conditions for up to 18 months (January 2023–June 2024) to 55 low-income transgender residents, with optional gender-affirming health care, case management and financial coaching. Funding: Public (city, county or state). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.kqed.org/news/11934949/gift-el-programa-de-san-francisco-que-otorgara-1200-al-mes-a-personas-transgenero ; https://ktvu.com/news/sf-launches-guaranteed-income-program-for-transgender-community
- NET (Nourish, Empower, Trust) Growth Movement (Alameda County, California, USA; 2023–2024): Run by Alameda County Social Services Agency, paid from county funds; designed by young people with experience of foster care. $1,000 a month with no conditions for 24 months (January 2023–December 2024) to 67 young people who had aged out of extended foster care, with optional case management and savings matches. Funding: Public (city, county or state). Result: Chapin Hall (January 2026, formative evaluation, self-reported; 26 and 23 survey respondents) reported that 73% were food insecure before the pilot, 27% while being paid and 44% in the six months after it ended. Economic hardships were also more common after payments stopped. No control group. Source: https://www.chapinhall.org/wp-content/uploads/Chapin-Hall_Alameda-Guaranteed-Income-Evaluation-Brief_Jan2026.pdf
- Pathway to Income Equity (Sonoma County, California, USA; 2023–2025): Run by First 5 Sonoma County, a public early-childhood agency, with Sonoma County and several cities, mostly paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA). $500 a month with no conditions for two years, from February 2023, to 305 low-income Sonoma County families with a baby on the way or a child under 6, chosen at random from 2,383 eligible families. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA), Public (city, county or state). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/sanfrancisco/news/sonoma-county-launches-guaranteed-income-pilot-program-for-low-income-families/ ; https://www.sonomanews.com/2022/09/05/pilot-program-for-guaranteed-income-begins-in-sonoma-county
- ARISE (Alexandria Recurring Income for Success and Equity) (Alexandria, Virginia, USA; 2023–2025): Run by City of Alexandria (Department of Community and Human Services), paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA) and then city money, with a randomized evaluation by Abt Global. $500 a month with no conditions for 29 months (February 2023–June 2025, extended from 24) to 170 low-income residents chosen at random from 4,149 eligible applicants. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA), Public (city, county or state). Result: Abt Global's final report (April 2026), compared with 210 controls: a statistically significant drop in homelessness by month 24, a significantly larger share able to cover costs and less use of payday loans, but no measurable gain in food security; changes in stress measures were modest. Source: https://alexandriava.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/ARISEAlexandriaFinalReportCompressed.pdf ; https://www.alexandriava.gov/go/6437
- Family Income for Empowerment Program (FIEP) (San Diego County, California, USA; 2023–): Run by County of San Diego (Child and Family Well-Being Department), paid from federal pandemic relief and run by Jewish Family Service of San Diego. $500 a month with no conditions for 24 months, from March 2023, to 408 low-income families referred by the county child welfare department (up to 452 planned), aiming to keep children out of foster care. Funding: Public (city, county or state). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.jfssd.org/programsreport ; https://jfssd.org/our-services/economic-mobility/family-income-for-empowerment-program
- Chicago Future Fund (Chicago, Illinois, USA; 2023–2024): Run by Equity and Transformation (EAT) Chicago, a nonprofit run by and for people affected by incarceration, with foundation support including the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation. $500 a month with no conditions for 12 months (March 2023–February 2024) to 100 formerly incarcerated people in three West and South Side neighborhoods (the fund's second round). Funding: Philanthropic. Result: An evaluation for EAT (report by Ashley Baber, published February 2025; 100 surveyed, 20 interviewed) reported late bill payments down 15 percentage points and homelessness in the prior month down 9 points from the start of the program, with 3 of 100 reporting recidivism; self-reported, with no control group. Source: https://www.rwjf.org/en/insights/our-research/2024/01/the-chicago-future-fund-building-economies-of-belonging.html ; https://citizennewspapergroup.com/news/2025/feb/19/eat-chicago-releases-new-report-on-guaranteed-income/
- Direct Cash Transfer Plus (DCT+) (Oregon, USA (Multnomah, Clackamas and Deschutes counties); 2023–2025): Run by The Oregon Department of Human Services' Youth Experiencing Homelessness Program, paid from the state budget, with the nonprofit Point Source Youth and three local youth groups. $1,000 a month with no conditions for two years (March 2023–March 2025), plus a one-time $3,000, to 120 homeless young people aged 18–24 in three Oregon counties, with optional housing and money-management support. Funding: Public (city, county or state). Result: Young People to the Front's final report (released January 2026) reported that 94% of the 63 youth who completed surveys said they were housed at the end, and 72% were working or in school; these are self-reported, with no control group and fewer than half the participants surveyed. Source: https://apps.oregon.gov/oregon-newsroom/OR/ODHS/Posts/Post/combination-of-cash-with-other-supports-proves-effective-in-helping-young-adults-out-of-homelessness-study-found ; https://www.opb.org/article/2024/01/26/homeless-youth-oregon-1000-dollars-a-month-support/
- Long Beach Pledge Guaranteed Income Pilot (Long Beach, California, USA; 2023–2025): Run by City of Long Beach, paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA) for the first cohort and city homelessness emergency funds for the second; the Fund for Guaranteed Income delivered payments. $500 a month with no conditions for 12 months to 450 families with children below the poverty line, in two cohorts: 250 in ZIP code 90813 (May 2023–April 2024) and 200 in five other ZIP codes (March 2024–February 2025). Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA), Public (city, county or state). Result: CSULB researchers (preliminary final report on cohort 1, September 2024) compared single-parent recipients with a randomly assigned control group: two months after payments ended, 44.6% vs 66.7% had cut meal sizes and 72.3% vs 50.0% had high-speed internet, with no significant effect on employment; self-reported surveys, 79 controls, 51–63% response. Source: https://www.longbeach.gov/edo/special-reports-and-publications/ ; https://longbeach.gov/press-releases/long-beach-pledge--guaranteed-income-pilot-application-now-open/
- Palm Springs Guaranteed Income Pilot (Palm Springs, California, USA; 2023–): Run by Two Palm Springs nonprofits, Queer Works and DAP Health, paid from city money; DAP Health took over in July 2024 after payment problems. $800 a month with no conditions for 18 months, from May 2023, to 30 low-income residents who are clients of the two nonprofits, chosen at random; transgender and nonbinary people were encouraged to apply. Funding: Public (city, county or state). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2024/jan/12/instagram-posts/no-a-california-city-is-not-giving-all-transgender/ ; https://www.yahoo.com/news/problems-palm-springs-basic-income-232308299.html
- Rise Up Cambridge (Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA; 2023–2024): Run by City of Cambridge, a citywide follow-up to the RISE pilot paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA). $500 a month with no conditions for 18 months from June 2023 to nearly 2,000 low-income families with children (at or below 250% of the federal poverty level). Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA). Result: MDRC (April 2026), from surveys and interviews with no control group: 93% of survey respondents used the money for food and 75% for emergencies, and 96% reported less stress while paid. For nearly half, the $500 plus household income still fell below the federal poverty line. Source: https://www.cambridgema.gov/news/2026/04/riseupcambridgeevaluationmeaningfulshorttermfinancialreliefforlowincomefamilies
- Quality Housing Coalition cash pilot for single mothers (Portland, Maine, USA; 2023–2024): Run by Quality Housing Coalition, a Portland nonprofit, paid from private donations and grants. $1,000 a month with no conditions for a year from June 2023 to 20 low-income single mothers, alongside social support; a second group of 20 began in September 2024. Funding: Philanthropic, Public (city, county or state). Result: The coalition's own study (September 2024), as reported by the Bangor Daily News, compared with a control group: the number saying they were doing OK or better financially rose from one to about half, while the control group stayed flat, and all participants stayed housed. Very small sample (n = 20). Source: https://www.bangordailynews.com/2024/02/05/state/state-housing/20-maine-mothers-given-1000-per-month-joam40zk0w ; https://www.bangordailynews.com/2024/09/10/business/experiment-maine-mothers-universal-basic-income-joam40zk0w
- GROW (Guaranteed Resources Optimize Wellbeing) Study (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; 2023–2024): Run by City of Philadelphia's Office of Community Empowerment and Opportunity, paid from existing Extended TANF funds (about $322,000), with payments delivered by the Fund for Guaranteed Income. $500 a month with no conditions for 12 months from June 2023 to 51 parents on Extended TANF, while 239 others in a randomized control group got $50 a month. Funding: Public (city, county or state). Result: Reinvestment Fund and University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee researchers (May 2026), compared with the $50 control group: modest but statistically significant gains in financial wellbeing, mental health and food insecurity, which returned to baseline or slightly worse after payments stopped. Small sample (51). Source: https://www.phila.gov/2023-08-11-city-launches-guaranteed-income-pilot-study-for-e-tanf-beneficiaries-in-philadelphia/ ; https://www.phillyvoice.com/philly-guaranteed-income-assistance-500-dollars-monthly-low-income-parents-grow-study/amp/
- United Way Guaranteed Income Program, City of Sacramento cohort (Sacramento, California, USA; 2023–2024): Run by United Way California Capital Region, paid from the City of Sacramento's federal pandemic relief (ARPA). $500 a month with no conditions for one year (July 2023–June 2024) to 80 low-income Sacramento households picked at random from nearly 13,000 applicants. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA). Result: Sacramento State (2025) reported that, by the end, 46% of recipients said they were financially better off vs 19% of the control group; 13% got an eviction or pay-rent notice vs 24%; recipients' food insecurity fell from 51% to 37%. - El Monte Guaranteed Income Pilot (El Monte, California, USA; 2023–2024): Run by City of El Monte, paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA); the RAND Corporation ran enrollment and the evaluation with USC. $500 a month with no conditions for a year (first payment July 2023, last scheduled May 31, 2024) to 125 low-income single mothers chosen from more than 2,500 applications. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA). Result: No published evaluation yet. - Rochester Guaranteed Basic Income Pilot (Rochester, New York, USA; 2023–2024): Run by City of Rochester, paid largely from federal COVID relief money, with a randomized study by Notre Dame's Wilson Sheehan Lab for Economic Opportunities. $500 a month with no conditions for 12 months to 351 low-income residents picked at random from 11,698 eligible applicants, in two cohorts paid between September 2023 and November 2024. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA). Result: Notre Dame researchers (reported December 2025), compared with applicants not selected: recipients were nearly three times as likely to have improved savings, 51% less likely to expect material hardship and 25% more likely to be driving a car at the end, with no difference in paying off past debt. Surveyed at the last payment, so no long-term effects; described as modest. Source: https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/14150 ; https://www.wxxinews.org/local-news/2025-12-30/guaranteed-basic-income-trial-program-in-rochester-led-to-modest-improvements-for-recipients-study-says

- Rx Kids (Flint, Michigan, USA (since expanded to about 42 Michigan communities, including Detroit); 2024–): Run by Michigan State University, with GiveDirectly delivering the money, funded by the State of Michigan and private donors. $1,500 during pregnancy and then $500 a month for the baby's first year, with no conditions or income test, to every mother in Flint from 2024; by May 2026 it had reached more than 11,000 families in 42 Michigan communities. Funding: Public (city, county or state), Philanthropic. Result: A Lancet Public Health study (May 2026; about 4,500 Flint births, 2021–mid-2025, compared with similar Michigan cities) estimated 18% fewer preterm births, 27% less low birthweight and about 29% fewer NICU admissions after the 2024 launch; quasi-experimental, by researchers from the program's own universities. Source: https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1129390 ; https://rxkids.org/
- In Her Hands (second cohort, Atlanta's west side) (Atlanta (Vine City and English Avenue), Georgia, USA; 2024–): Run by Georgia Resilience and Opportunity Fund (GRO Fund), expanded with a $6.2 million grant from the Arthur M. Blank Family Foundation. An average of $1,000 a month with no conditions for 36 months from 2024 to 270 women on Atlanta's west side, with the option of a smaller monthly amount plus a lump sum. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://policiesforaction.org/blog/her-hands-path-financial-security-black-women-georgia ; https://atlanta.capitalbnews.org/guaranteed-income-atlanta
- Humboldt Income Program (Humboldt County, California, USA; 2024–2025): Run by McKinleyville Family Resource Center, a nonprofit, with a California state grant and local donations. $920 a month with no conditions for 18 months to 150 low-income pregnant people in Humboldt County, from January 2024; another 100 applicants were randomly assigned to get $20 a month as a control group. Funding: Public (city, county or state), Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.northcoastjournal.com/news-2/guaranteed-income-28905899/ ; https://cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/guaranteed-income-pilot-program/pregnant-individuals-and-former-foster-youth
- Inland SoCal United Way Guaranteed Income Pilot (Riverside and San Bernardino counties, California, USA; 2024): Run by Inland Southern California United Way, the largest of California's seven state-funded guaranteed income pilots, with county and foundation money. $600 a month with no conditions for 12 months, from January 2024, to 409 pregnant people in Riverside County, plus $750 a month for 18 months to 35 former foster youth in Riverside and San Bernardino counties. Funding: Public (city, county or state), Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/guaranteed-income-pilot-program/pregnant-individuals-and-former-foster-youth ; https://laist.com/brief/news/guaranteed-income-in-ie
- Guaranteed Income to Grow Ann Arbor (GIG A2) (Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; 2024–2025): Run by City of Ann Arbor, paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA); the University of Michigan's Poverty Solutions ran and evaluated it. $528 a month with no conditions for two years (January 2024–December 2025) to 100 low-income entrepreneurs and gig workers chosen at random from over 1,000 applicants; another 100 got $25 a month as a comparison group. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA). Result: U-M Poverty Solutions' Year 1 report (January 2026, 100 recipients vs 100 comparison) found no statistically significant differences in food, housing or utility insecurity after one year; both groups had food insecurity of 58–61%. Recipients said they spent mostly on food (68%) and household supplies (60%), and interviewees described less stress. Preliminary; final report due in 2026. Source: https://poverty.umich.edu/files/2026/01/GIGA2-Year-1-report-final.pdf ; https://a2independent.com/2024/01/23/ann-arbors-guaranteed-income-program-starts-giving-out-528-monthly-payments/
- Elevate Boulder (Boulder, Colorado, USA; 2024–2025): Run by The City of Boulder, paid mainly from federal pandemic relief (ARPA), with help from the Community Foundation Boulder County and private donors. $500 a month with no strings attached for two years (from January 2024) to 200 low-income Boulder households. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA), Philanthropic. Result: An evaluation by the Omni Institute (September 2025, first 20 months, surveys of participants before and during the program) reported significantly less psychological distress and food insecurity and easier rent and utility payments; there was no significant change in employment, savings, debt or the ability to cover a $400 expense, and there was no control group. Source: https://bouldercolorado.gov/news/city-boulder-releases-evaluation-report-guaranteed-income-pilot-project ; https://www.aol.com/articles/colorado-city-gave-low-income-194841028.html
- Pregnancy Assistance Income with Dignity (P.A.I.D.) (Los Angeles County, California, USA; 2024–2025): Run by National Council of Jewish Women, Los Angeles, with a grant from California's state-funded guaranteed income pilot program. $1,000 a month with no conditions for 18 months, from April 2024, to 180 randomly selected low-income pregnant people in Los Angeles County. Funding: Public (city, county or state). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/guaranteed-income-pilot-program/pregnant-individuals-and-former-foster-youth ; https://ilponline.org/Uploads/1341_Leave_Behind_PAID_Flyer.2024.pdf
- Thrive Prince George's (Prince George's County, Maryland, USA; 2024–2026): Run by Greater Washington Community Foundation, with funding from Prince George's County and the Meyer Foundation. $800 a month with no conditions for 24 months from April 2024 to 175 people: 125 low-income seniors and 50 young adults who aged out of foster care. Funding: Public (city, county or state), Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.thecommunityfoundation.org/news/thrive-prince-georges-guaranteed-income-pilot-begins-monthly-cash-payments
- The Bridge Project in Milwaukee (Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; 2024–): Run by The Bridge Project, a New York-born nonprofit program, with Milwaukee's Zilber Family Foundation and later public money. $1,125 before birth, then $750 a month for 15 months and $375 a month for 21 months (three years in all) with no strings attached, from June 2024, to 122 low-income pregnant women in four Milwaukee ZIP codes chosen by lottery. Funding: Philanthropic, Public (city, county or state). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://zilberfamilyfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/ZFF_BridgeProject-FactSheetUpdated-250826-v5.pdf
- Advancing Fresno County Guaranteed Income (Fresno and Huron, Fresno County, California, USA; 2024–2025): Run by Fresno Economic Opportunities Commission, a local anti-poverty agency, paid for by private foundations. $500 a month with no conditions for 12 months (July 2024–June 2025) to 150 low-income families with young children, 75 in southwest Fresno and 75 in rural Huron, chosen by lottery. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: Fresno State's Center for Community Voices (December 2025; randomized trial with 300 families) reported that borrowing for regular expenses fell from 40% to 18%, along with less food insecurity and parental stress, and no significant effect on employment. Source: https://fresnoeoc.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Fresno-EOC-AGI-Final-Word-Press-Release-2025.pdf ; https://fresnoeoc.org/guaranteed-income/
- Somerville Guaranteed Basic Income Pilot (Somerville, Massachusetts, USA; 2024–2025): Run by City of Somerville, paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA), evaluated by UMass Boston's Collins Center. $750 a month with no conditions on a reloadable debit card for 12 months (July 2024–June 2025) to 198 households at high risk of losing their housing. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA), Philanthropic. Result: UMass Boston's Collins Center (2026), comparing participants before and after with no control group: the share who rarely or never had money left at month's end fell from 73% to 55%, and 66% of the 33 households behind on rent caught up. Self-reported. Source: https://www.somervillema.gov/departments/somerville-guaranteed-basic-income-pilot
- UpTogether Illinois guaranteed income pilot (Downstate Illinois (Peoria, Carbondale, Springfield, Bloomington, Normal, Champaign, Rockford, Belleville and East St. Louis), USA; 2024–2025): Run by UpTogether, a national nonprofit, paid for by a private donor, to build the case for a statewide program. $500 a month with no conditions for one year from September 2024 to 52 families in nine downstate Illinois cities, including Peoria and Rockford. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.northernpublicradio.org/illinois/2025-02-07/familes-from-peoria-other-illinois-cities-are-getting-500-a-month-as-part-of-guaranteed-income-pilot
- Nurturing Futures (Boulder County, Colorado, USA; 2024–): Run by Boulder County's Department of Human Services, paid from federal pandemic relief (ARPA), with AidKit helping with applications. $300 a month with no spending restrictions for two years, from October 2024, to 725 Boulder County households with a child under 4 and income below 30% of the area median, chosen by lottery; in May 2026 the county voted to continue it at $600 a month. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://bouldercounty.gov/news/new-6-million-direct-cash-assistance-program-for-families-with-young-children/ ; https://bouldercounty.gov/news/nurturing-futures-direct-cash-assistance-to-continue-with-increased-payments/
- BOOST (Building Outstanding Opportunities for Students to Thrive) (Los Angeles, California, USA; 2024–2025): Run by Los Angeles Community College District, paid with private money from the Broad Foundation and the California Community Foundation's Young Adults Forward Fund. $1,000 a month with no conditions for 12 months (November 2024–October 2025) to 251 low-income community college students in health-career programs; over 300 others formed a comparison group. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://guaranteedincome.us/los-angeles-boost ; https://laist.com/news/education/laccd-guaranteed-basic-income-update
- Ohio Mothers Trust (Columbus, Ohio, USA; 2024–2025): Run by Three nonprofits (RISE Together Innovation Institute, Motherful and UpTogether), paid with $211,200 of their own and donor money. $500 a month with no conditions for 12 months from December 2024 to 32 single mothers in Columbus. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://blog.uptogether.org/first-ever-unconditional-guaranteed-income-initiative-launches-in-columbus
- Uplift Salem (Salem, Massachusetts, USA; 2024–2025): Run by City of Salem with the nonprofit UpTogether, paid from federal COVID relief and private money, studied by Salem State University. $500 a month with no conditions for a year (December 2024–November 2025) to 100 residents living at or below the poverty line, chosen by lottery. Funding: Federal pandemic relief (ARPA), Philanthropic. Result: Salem State University researchers' preliminary findings (March 2026), self-reported by participants: 37% strongly agreed they were better prepared for unexpected challenges at the end, up 10 points from August, and about three-quarters of parents spent more time with their children. A final report was due later. Source: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2024/10/17/metro/massachusetts-salem-basic-income-cash-poverty ; https://www.salemstate.edu/news/uplift-salem-north-shore-policy-lab-share-insights-findings-income-pilot
- The Bridge Project (Appalachia) (Appalachian Kentucky, Ohio and West Virginia, USA; 2025–): Run by The Bridge Project, started by the New York-based Monarch Foundation. $1,125 during pregnancy, then $750 a month for 15 months and $375 a month for 21 months with no conditions, from April 2025, to 500 low-income mothers in Appalachian Kentucky, Ohio and West Virginia; 750 others get small payments for surveys. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.reviewonline.com/news/local-news/2025/01/bridge-project-offering-help-for-expecting-mothers/
- IndyEast Guaranteed Income Initiative (Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; 2025–): Run by Three east-side Indianapolis community centers, funded by a $2.5 million United Way of Central Indiana grant. $500 a month for 18 months from October 2025, with optional coaching, to 25 east-side households picked at random from the centers' clients; the goal is 125 households by 2026. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.wrtv.com/news/local-news/in-your-community/east-side-indy/indyeast-guaranteed-income-initiative-helps-families-with-500-monthly-payments
- ROOTED (Resources & Opportunities for Ongoing Transition, Empowerment & Dignity) (Durham, North Carolina, USA; 2026–): Run by City of Durham (Community Safety Department), with $1 million from the city council after the Excel pilot; evaluated by Duke University researchers. $8,400 over a year with no conditions ($700 a month, or larger early payments that taper) in 2026 to 107 formerly incarcerated Durham residents chosen by lottery; unselected applicants form the comparison group. Funding: Public (city, county or state). Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.wunc.org/term/news/2026-07-08/guaranteed-income-reentry-incarceration-durham-mecklenburg ; https://www.northcarolinahealthnews.org/2026/07/06/two-nc-local-governments-test-guaranteed-income-formerly-incarcerated/
- AI Dividend (Run by US nonprofits, for people whose work has been hurt by AI; 2026–): Run by What We Will (an advocacy group for AI-affected workers) and the AI Commons Project, part of the Fund for Guaranteed Income, which funds it. $1,000 a month with no strings attached for a year, alongside reskilling, to a first cohort of 25–50 workers hurt by AI, selected on a rolling basis; the first payments went out in March 2026. Funding: Philanthropic. Result: No published evaluation yet. Source: https://www.bloodinthemachine.com/p/the-first-basic-income-for-workers

## Cash-out ranking

All 40 services on this site, ranked by a cash-out score (our rating). The score is calculated automatically from the facts shown on each service page: cash-out, market price, operator, ease, whether it is invite-only and when it was last checked. This is not a list of services we cashed out ourselves. Cash-out rules and prices change often, so always check the official information before you sign up. Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/ranking/

Scoring (out of 100): Cash-out (can it become cash, e-money or gift cards?): yes 40, with conditions 20, no or not verified 0; Is the value clear? The token has a market price, or it is not crypto and pays in money or points: 15; partly: 8; no or not verified: 0; Is the operator public? Public 15, partly 8, unknown 0; Ease (1 to 5, our own judgement) × 3 (up to 15); You can start without an invitation: 10; Recently checked (within 3 months of the newest check month on the site): 5. The groups follow the cash-out rating (yes → easy, with conditions → with conditions, no or not verified → hard or unclear). A service with a strong warning goes into “hard or unclear” whatever its score. Within a group, higher scores come first; ties keep the order of the main list. Raffles, where only winners get paid, go into their own group after “with conditions”, even when cash-out is “yes”. Services that pay only people chosen as recipients (for example from a waiting list) go into “with conditions” even when cash-out is “yes”, because signing up does not mean you will be paid.

## Graveyard

A record of services and programmes that once handed out money or points and have since ended. Only endings confirmed by an official announcement or a credible source are listed. Thanks for the lunches. Rest in peace.

### Thailand — 10,000-Baht Digital Wallet

- Ended: 2025-05-19
- Source: The Nation (Thailand), https://www.nationthailand.com/news/policy/40050186
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-thailand-digital-wallet

What it was: Thailand’s plan to give 10,000 baht each to about 50 million people aged 16+ through a digital wallet that could only be spent locally; some Japanese media called it a basic income

Ended: The third round, the first meant to use the wallet (about 2.7 million people aged 16–20), was postponed indefinitely on 19 May 2025 (“not a cancellation,” said the finance minister). The two earlier rounds (Sep 2024, Jan 2025) were paid as one-off cash into bank accounts. In Nov 2025 the Finance Ministry said no new handout had been announced

Why: The 157 billion baht set aside for the handouts was moved to other measures as US tariffs clouded the economy (water, transport, tourism, help for exporters and SMEs, jobs); the NESDC planning agency and the Bank of Thailand had advised reviewing the handout

### World — WLD Airdrop (Grants)

- Ended: 2026-06-01
- Source: World Help Center, https://support.world.org/hc/en-us/articles/30969185598739-Updates-to-the-Airdrop-Program
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-wld-airdrop

What it was: Monthly WLD token airdrops (formerly grants) for people who proved they are human with World ID

Ended: No new or renewed cycles from 1 June 2026 (existing 12-month cycles can still be claimed until they end)

Why: The official help page gives no reason; it only says airdrop cycles are no longer being created or renewed

### Miles

- Ended: 2025-05-14
- Source: note (Yuhki Ogasawara), https://note.com/y121516/n/nbb9bf7625c03
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-miles

What it was: An app that earned miles just by carrying your phone as you travelled, redeemable for goods and gift cards (run in Japan by Miles Japan)

Ended: 14 May 2025 (announced by email the same day, with no grace period)

Why: Officially only called a “difficult decision”; no reason was given

### My Basic Income

- Ended: 2017
- Source: Business Insider (syndicated), https://www.pulse.com.gh/bi/tech/tech-a-dollar15000-basic-income-lottery-promised-free-money-for-a-year-then-the/5gbp5pj
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-mybasicincome

What it was: A San Francisco group that raffled off a crowdfunded one-year basic income of $15,000 (2016)

Ended: Around 2017 (the winner received only 5 of 12 payments and no second raffle followed; the website was offline as of Oct 2026)

Why: Delayed and missed payments were reported; no official explanation was found

### ME Token (RewardMe)

- Ended: 2025-07
- Source: RewardMe Help, https://help.reward.me/en/articles/4901904-sunsetting-me-token-jul-2025
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-me-token

What it was: The reward token of the cashback app RewardMe

Ended: Retired in July 2025 (balances were automatically converted 1:1 into Reward Dollars)

Why: The official help page gives no reason

### RewardMe (Philippines)

- Ended: 2025-12-31
- Source: RewardMe Help, https://help.reward.me/en/articles/12780396-winding-down-operations-in-the-philippines
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-rewardme-ph

What it was: The cashback app RewardMe’s service in the Philippines

Ended: Cashback ended on 10 Dec 2025, and MDT withdrawals and conversions on 31 Dec 2025 (gift-card redemption only after that)

Why: The official notice gives no reason
